title: An Offer of Wings
text: A tall thing with too many feathers stands in the path. It looks you over, all of you, the way a buyer looks over stock at a fair, counting teeth. Its eyes settle on the lightest of you. It wants them, it says, and it will pay in wings.

options.label: Let it choose the lightest of you, and pay whatever price comes with wings.

outcomes.text: It wraps the one it chose in its wings, and when it lets go they move like wind. They do not say what they saw inside the feathers.
It takes something in trade and will not say what. They feel lighter, and emptier, and cannot remember a thing they used to know.

options.label: Tell it no, and hold your ground. Your own are not for sale.

outcomes.text: It shrugs, all its feathers at once, and is gone. One feather stays caught on the Leader's collar, and they are light on their feet for the next fight.
It does not like that answer. All its feathers rise at once.

options.label: The Vagabond haggles it down to a single feather, with a grin and a bold tongue.

outcomes.text: It is so charmed by the cheek of it that it pays the Vagabond for the pleasure of being haggled with: one feather, and the light step that goes with it.
